questions.question: At Seaview Resort, managers greet employees by name, celebrate staff who go above and beyond for guests, and encourage everyone to suggest improvements. New hires quickly learn that guest service and teamwork are expected. These practices help create
questions.explanation: A positive culture. Daily habits, such as recognition, respect, and openness to ideas, shape a culture in which employees feel valued and understand what matters most. A positive culture often leads to better service and lower turnover. Nothing in the situation describes a strict chain of command, and these practices usually reduce rather than increase turnover. Dress code is a separate policy that isn't mentioned. A positive culture can also help businesses attract new employees, since workers often share their experiences online.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of organizational culture

questions.question: Why do airlines often charge higher prices for tickets bought a few days before a flight?

options.C: Planes cost more to fly on short notice
options.D: Fuel is cheaper for early bookings

questions.explanation: Last-minute travelers often pay more. Travelers who buy at the last minute, such as business travelers or people with emergencies, often have little flexibility and are willing to pay more. Airlines use this to set higher prices close to departure. The cost of operating the flight doesn't change much, airlines want full planes, and fuel costs aren't tied to when a ticket was bought. This pricing approach is part of revenue management. Leisure travelers who book early often get lower fares because they can choose flights when seats are less in demand.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of price in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A caller tells the Lakeside Hotel's front desk clerk that he stayed at the hotel last week and wants to confirm a charge. He asks the clerk to read back the full credit card number on file so he can check which card was used. What should the clerk do?

options.B: Read the full number to be helpful
options.C: Email the number to the caller
options.D: Read only the first twelve digits

questions.explanation: Refuse and verify the caller. Hotels should never read full card numbers over the phone, because the caller could be a thief. Clerks should follow verification procedures and, if needed, confirm only limited information, such as the last four digits. Reading the full number, emailing it, or giving most of the digits could help a criminal commit fraud. Protecting customer data is both an ethical duty and a requirement of payment security rules. If the caller is the real guest, the clerk can suggest he check his own card statements or provide the last four digits after verifying his identity.

performanceIndicator.text: Comply with strategies to protect digital customer data (e.g., information about customers, customers' credit-card numbers, passwords, customer transactions)

questions.question: Under the Americans with Disabilities Act, a restaurant must generally allow a guest's trained service dog to

options.A: enter only when the restaurant is empty.
options.B: accompany the guest in the dining area.
options.C: enter only if the guest pays a fee.
options.D: stay outside in the parking lot.

questions.explanation: Accompany the guest in the dining area. The ADA generally requires businesses open to the public, including restaurants, to allow service animals to go wherever customers are allowed. Businesses can't charge extra fees for service animals or limit their entry to certain times. Staff may ask only limited questions, such as whether the animal is required because of a disability. Following these rules protects guests' rights and helps the business avoid discrimination complaints. Businesses can't require documentation for a service animal, though they can ask a guest to remove an animal that is out of control.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the rights of customers in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Which of the following is an effective conflict-resolution strategy:

options.B: Focusing on the problem, not the person
options.C: Insisting that the other person is wrong
options.D: Raising your voice to make a point

questions.explanation: Focusing on the problem, not the person. Focusing on the problem keeps the discussion productive and avoids personal attacks that make people defensive. Raising your voice escalates tension, avoiding the issue lets it grow, and insisting the other person is wrong prevents compromise. Effective conflict resolution also involves listening, finding common goals, and agreeing on a solution. When people feel heard and respected, they are more willing to work toward a solution together. Using "I" statements, such as "I'm concerned about the deadline," can also keep conversations from becoming personal attacks.

performanceIndicator.text: Use conflict-resolution skills

questions.question: Eli, an event coordinator, has three weddings next month and keeps missing small deadlines with vendors. Which approach would best help him manage his time?

options.A: Rely on memory for each deadline
options.C: Handle each vendor only when they call
options.D: Use a shared calendar with reminders

questions.explanation: Use a shared calendar with reminders. A calendar with reminders keeps all deadlines in one place and alerts Eli before they arrive, so he can plan his work. Memory is unreliable with many details, waiting for vendors to call means he is always reacting rather than planning, and working longer without a plan doesn't fix the underlying organization problem. Good time management is especially important when managing several events at once. He could also set aside time each morning to review upcoming deadlines for all three weddings.

performanceIndicator.text: Use time-management skills

questions.question: A hotel's sales manager needs to send a written proposal to a corporate client describing room rates, meeting space, and catering options for a three-day conference. Which format should she use?
questions.explanation: A formal business proposal. A formal proposal organizes detailed information, such as prices, services, and terms, in a professional format the client can review, share, and keep for reference. Text messages and sticky notes are too informal and limited for a complex offer, and a personal social media post is inappropriate for confidential business information. Choosing a professional format also signals that the hotel takes the client's business seriously. The proposal can also include photos of the meeting rooms and a clear deadline for the client to respond.

performanceIndicator.text: Select and utilize appropriate formats for professional writing

questions.question: Why do many hospitality businesses experience large changes in demand during the year?

options.A: Restaurants serve the same number of meals daily
options.B: Travel often depends on seasons and holidays
options.C: Customers travel the same amount every week
options.D: Hotels close every winter by law

questions.explanation: Travel often depends on seasons and holidays. Demand for hospitality services often rises during summer vacations, school breaks, holidays, and local events, and falls during off-seasons. A beach resort may be full in July and nearly empty in January, while a ski lodge sees the opposite pattern. Customers don't travel the same amount each week, no law requires hotels to close in winter, and restaurant traffic varies by day and season. Businesses manage these changes with flexible staffing and seasonal pricing.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Several resort towns are limiting short-term vacation rentals, raising tourist taxes, and capping the number of cruise ship visitors because residents complain about crowds, traffic, and rising housing costs. This trend is often described as a response to
questions.explanation: Overtourism. Overtourism occurs when too many visitors overwhelm a destination, harming residents' quality of life and sometimes the environment. Many cities are responding with limits and fees. Space tourism involves commercial spaceflight, agritourism brings visitors to farms, and medical tourism involves traveling for health care. Hospitality businesses need to watch issues like overtourism because new rules can affect how they operate. Hotels, tour operators, and cruise lines in these destinations may face new fees or limits on how many guests they can serve.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe current issues and trends in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Which of the following is a possible drawback of automating guest services with kiosks and apps:

options.B: Some guests may want personal help
options.C: Staff have more time for other tasks

questions.explanation: Some guests may want personal help. Automation brings benefits such as faster check-in, more staff time for complex requests, and fewer data-entry errors. However, some guests, such as those who are less comfortable with technology or who have special needs, prefer speaking with a person. Businesses that automate services should still make friendly, knowledgeable employees easy to reach. The other options describe advantages, not drawbacks. Many hotels keep a staffed desk next to their kiosks for exactly this reason.

performanceIndicator.text: Use software to automate services

questions.question: A popular steakhouse begins selling its signature seasonings and steak sauces online. What is a risk of this product extension?

options.B: The restaurant must close its dining room
options.D: Poor quality could hurt its reputation

questions.explanation: Poor quality could hurt its reputation. When a brand extends into new products, the new products are tied to the original brand. If the sauces are poor quality or hard to get, customers may think less of the restaurant itself. Online sales are possible, extending the product doesn't require closing the dining room, and no extension guarantees profits. Businesses reduce this risk by testing new products and keeping quality consistent with the brand. The restaurant must also make sure its staff and kitchens can handle the extra work without hurting service to diners.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of product extensions in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A family with two young children asks the front desk agent for suggestions for a rainy afternoon. Which recommendation best meets their needs?
questions.explanation: A nearby indoor children's museum. The best recommendation fits the family's situation: they need something indoors because of the rain, suitable for young children, and available in the afternoon. A children's museum meets all three needs. A jazz club is for adults at night, a wine tour isn't appropriate for young children, and an outdoor garden would be uncomfortable in the rain. Listening carefully and asking questions lead to better recommendations. The agent might also mention a backup option, such as an indoor play center, in case the museum is crowded.

performanceIndicator.text: Recommend hospitality and tourism services

questions.question: Which of the following is an effective time-management technique:

options.A: Waiting until the deadline to begin

questions.explanation: Prioritizing tasks by importance. Prioritizing helps people focus on the tasks that matter most and are due soonest. Doing only easy tasks can leave important work undone, trying to do everything at once leads to mistakes and stress, and waiting until the deadline leaves no time to fix problems. Lists, calendars, and breaking large tasks into steps also help with time management. Many people find it helpful to identify their top three priorities at the start of each day.

performanceIndicator.text: Use time-management skills

questions.question: A survey of visitors to Cedar Falls State Park shows that most chose the park because of its hiking trails, waterfalls, and quiet campgrounds away from city noise. These visitors are mainly motivated by
questions.explanation: Nature and relaxation. The features visitors mentioned, such as trails, waterfalls, and quiet campsites, appeal to people who want to enjoy nature and escape busy city life. Nightlife, business meetings, and shopping are motivations for other types of trips, such as city vacations or conferences. Knowing what motivates visitors helps the park plan services and promotions that attract similar guests. For example, the park might promote quiet weekday camping or guided nature walks to reach more visitors with the same interests.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain factors that motivate people to choose a hospitality and tourism site

questions.question: When conducting a risk assessment for an outdoor festival, organizers should first
questions.explanation: Identify what could go wrong. A risk assessment starts by identifying possible hazards, such as severe weather, crowd injuries, food safety problems, or lost children. Organizers then rate how likely and serious each risk is and plan ways to reduce or respond to them. Printing tickets, choosing music, and hiring a photographer are planning tasks, but they don't help organizers understand or prepare for risks. Without this first step, organizers might spend money on details while missing a serious danger.

performanceIndicator.text: Conduct a risk assessment of an event

questions.question: Housekeepers at a large hotel are negotiating a new union contract. They want lighter room quotas, while management wants to control costs. Which approach is most likely to lead to an agreement?

options.C: Refusing to meet with the union
options.D: Ignoring the contract until it expires

questions.explanation: Collective bargaining. Collective bargaining brings union representatives and management together to negotiate terms both sides can accept, such as a moderate change in room quotas combined with other adjustments. Firing workers for union activity is generally illegal, refusing to bargain violates labor law, and ignoring the contract could lead to a strike or legal action. Good-faith negotiation protects both the workers and the hotel's operations. Both sides usually make compromises, such as adjusting quotas while agreeing to new productivity tools.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain labor-relations issues

questions.question: Which of the following is an ethical practice in the hospitality industry:

options.A: Clearly listing all fees when guests book
options.B: Posting fake reviews of the business online

questions.explanation: Clearly listing all fees when guests book. Ethical hospitality businesses are honest with guests about prices and conditions. Listing all fees, such as resort or cleaning fees, at the time of booking lets guests know what they will pay. Surprise charges, fake reviews, and hidden inspection results mislead guests and can lead to lost trust, fines, and lawsuits. Honest practices build a reputation that brings guests back. Many travelers now share their experiences online, so businesses that treat guests honestly are more likely to earn positive reviews.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the role of ethics in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: Which of the following is an issue many hospitality businesses currently face:

options.A: Too many applicants for every job
options.C: A lack of travel demand worldwide

questions.explanation: Staffing shortages. Many hotels, restaurants, and airlines have struggled to hire and keep enough workers, which affects service and costs. Businesses have responded with higher pay, flexible schedules, and technology such as self-service kiosks. Too many applicants is the opposite of the current problem, most customers prefer online booking, and global travel demand has been strong. Staffing shortages can lead to longer waits and lower guest satisfaction, so many businesses are investing in training and better benefits to keep good employees.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe current issues and trends in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a project in the hospitality industry:
questions.explanation: Renovating a hotel's lobby. A project is a temporary effort with a defined beginning, end, and goal, such as renovating a lobby, opening a new restaurant, or planning a festival. Cleaning rooms, answering calls, and serving breakfast are ongoing operations that repeat every day. Project management tools help teams plan tasks, budgets, and deadlines for one-time efforts like renovations. Because renovations disrupt guests, project managers often schedule them during slower seasons. Projects like this need a budget, a timeline, and a team, and they end when the new lobby opens.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of project management

questions.question: The marketing manager of Harbor Lights Hotel uses the hotel's database to compare guests who booked directly through the hotel's website with guests who booked through online travel agencies. She finds that direct bookers spend 25% more on dining and are twice as likely to return within a year. The hotel also pays agencies a commission of about 15% on each booking. How might she use this analysis?

options.A: Promote direct booking on the website

questions.explanation: Promote direct booking on the website. The analysis shows that direct bookers are more valuable to the hotel, so encouraging more guests to book directly, perhaps with special offers, could increase revenue. Stopping online reservations would lose business, closing the restaurant would eliminate the spending the analysis highlights, and deleting data removes information the hotel may need later. Database analysis is most useful when it guides decisions like this. Because direct bookers spend more and the hotel avoids agency commissions, encouraging direct booking can increase profit in two ways.

performanceIndicator.text: Use database for information analysis

questions.question: Hannah owns a 30-room inn and is applying for a $150,000 bank loan to renovate. Occupancy last year was 58%, but the loan officer mentioned that applicants with occupancy above 65% are usually approved. Hannah is tempted to report 66% because she expects business to improve after the renovation. What should she do?

options.A: Ask her accountant to change the records

questions.explanation: Report the actual occupancy rates. Providing false information to a lender is unethical and can be illegal loan fraud. The owner should report accurate numbers and explain her plans for improving occupancy. Raising the numbers, leaving out slow months, or asking an accountant to change records are all forms of misrepresentation. Honest reporting protects her reputation and her ability to borrow in the future. Lenders often verify information, so false numbers could also lead to the loan being denied or canceled.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the role of ethics in finance

questions.question: Because hospitality services are intangible, businesses often help customers judge quality by
questions.explanation: Showing photos and guest reviews. Customers can't touch or try a hotel stay or a tour before buying it, so businesses use photos, videos, reviews, and awards to make the experience easier to imagine and evaluate. Refusing to share information or hiding prices would make customers less likely to buy. Services can't be returned after they are used. Reducing uncertainty is a key part of marketing hospitality products. Hotels also use virtual tours, ratings from travel websites, and guarantees to reduce guests' uncertainty.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of product in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A signature card at a bank is used to

options.D: record the amount of each deposit.

questions.explanation: Verify who can sign checks. When a business opens a bank account, authorized signers sign a signature card. The bank uses it to confirm that checks and withdrawals are approved by the right people, which helps prevent fraud. Deposit amounts are recorded on deposit slips, interest is calculated by the bank's systems, and daily sales are tracked in the business's own records. Signature cards are one of several cash control procedures. Businesses should update signature cards when authorized signers leave the company so former employees can't access accounts.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain cash control procedures (e.g., signature cards, deposit slips, internal/external controls, cash clearing, etc.)

questions.question: Why do many restaurants use standardized recipes?

options.C: To make every dish taste different

questions.explanation: To keep food quality consistent. Standardized recipes list exact ingredients, amounts, and steps, so every cook prepares a dish the same way. This keeps taste, portion size, and cost consistent, which is a key part of quality management. The goal is consistency, not variety in each serving. Recipes make training easier rather than eliminating it, and they reduce rather than increase waste by controlling portions. Standardized recipes also make it easier for new cooks to learn the menu and for managers to calculate food costs accurately.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of quality management

questions.question: A café cashier started her shift with a $150 cash fund in her drawer. At closing, the register report shows cash sales of $612, and she counts $755 in the drawer. She did not remove any cash during her shift. What is the result of reconciling the drawer?
questions.explanation: The drawer is $7 short. The drawer should contain the starting fund plus cash sales: $150 + $612 = $762. The cashier counted $755, which is $762 - $755 = $7 less than expected, so the drawer is $7 short. It is not over, and it doesn't balance. The $143 figure comes from comparing the count with sales only and forgetting the starting fund. The manager should investigate possible causes, such as an error in making change.

performanceIndicator.text: Reconcile cash

questions.question: A labor-relations issue arises when

options.A: workers and managers disagree on conditions.
options.D: a customer complains about a meal.

questions.explanation: Workers and managers disagree on conditions. Labor relations involve the relationship between employers and employees, often represented by unions, about matters such as wages, hours, benefits, and safety. Disagreements about working conditions are labor-relations issues. Customer complaints are customer-service issues, late deliveries are supply-chain issues, and a competitor's price cut is a market issue. Hotels, airlines, and casinos often have unionized workforces, so labor relations are important in hospitality. Labor-relations issues are often addressed through union contracts that spell out pay, hours, and grievance procedures.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain labor-relations issues

questions.question: During a severe thunderstorm, a theme park's lightning detection system shows strikes within five miles. What should employees do?

options.A: Wait until it starts raining heavily to act
options.B: Close rides and move guests to shelter
options.C: Keep rides running but warn guests
options.D: Move guests to open grassy areas

questions.explanation: Close rides and move guests to shelter. Lightning can strike miles from a storm, so parks follow procedures to stop outdoor rides and move guests into buildings when lightning is nearby. Warning guests while rides keep running exposes them to danger, waiting for heavy rain ignores the actual threat, and open grassy areas are among the most dangerous places to be during lightning. Following the emergency plan protects guests and employees. Parks usually wait until no lightning has been detected nearby for a set period, often 30 minutes, before reopening rides.

performanceIndicator.text: Handle emergency situations in hospitality and tourism

questions.question: Which of the following businesses is part of the recreation segment of the hospitality and tourism industry:
questions.explanation: An amusement park. The hospitality and tourism industry is often divided into segments such as lodging, food and beverage, travel and transportation, and recreation. Recreation businesses provide entertainment and leisure activities, such as amusement parks, golf courses, ski resorts, and museums. Banks, factories, and law firms may serve travelers occasionally, but they belong to finance, manufacturing, and legal services rather than hospitality and tourism. Recreation businesses often work closely with lodging and food businesses, such as resorts that combine rooms, restaurants, and golf courses in one package.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: The Westridge Hotel's records show that a frequent guest always requests a high floor and extra pillows. When she books again, the hotel prepares her room with both before she arrives. This is an example of

options.D: ignoring the customer data it has.

questions.explanation: Using CRM to personalize service. CRM systems store guests' preferences so employees can meet them without being asked. Preparing the room in advance makes the guest feel recognized and valued, which builds loyalty. The hotel isn't raising prices, it is using rather than ignoring data, and nothing suggests a policy change. Personalized service like this is a major reason guests return to the same hotel. CRM data should be kept accurate and private so guests trust the hotel with their information.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of customer relationship management

questions.question: Which of the following is a cash control procedure that a restaurant should use:

options.A: Letting each server keep their own cash
options.B: Two people counting cash at closing
options.C: Making deposits only once a month
options.D: Storing cash in an unlocked drawer

questions.explanation: Two people counting cash at closing. Having two employees count cash together, and record the total, makes errors and theft less likely and easier to detect. Letting servers hold cash without tracking it, making deposits infrequently, and leaving cash unlocked all increase the risk of loss. Good cash controls also include regular bank deposits, locked safes, and comparing register totals with sales records each day. These procedures protect honest employees too, because clear records show that cash was handled correctly.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain cash control procedures (e.g., signature cards, deposit slips, internal/external controls, cash clearing, etc.)

questions.question: An ethical dilemma occurs when

options.A: a decision has only one clear right answer.
options.D: a manager makes a routine decision.

questions.explanation: Choices conflict with personal values. In an ethical dilemma, each choice has some ethical cost, such as loyalty to a friend versus honesty with an employer. Dilemmas are hard precisely because there isn't one obviously right answer. A decision with one clear right answer, following the law, and routine decisions don't involve conflicting values. Recognizing dilemmas helps employees slow down, gather information, and seek advice. For example, an employee might feel torn between keeping a coworker's secret and reporting a safety problem.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain reasons for ethical dilemmas

questions.question: Which of the following is a risk that digital communication creates for a business:

options.B: Messages can be forwarded to unintended readers
options.D: Messages always arrive more slowly than letters

questions.explanation: Messages can be forwarded to unintended readers. Emails, texts, and chats can be forwarded, copied, or captured in screenshots in seconds, so information meant for one person can quickly reach customers, competitors, or the public. That is why businesses train employees to write carefully and avoid sharing confidential details. Digital messages are usually faster than letters, can include attachments, and make it easier, not harder, to communicate across locations. Digital messages can also be retrieved later in lawsuits or investigations, so employees should avoid writing anything they wouldn't want shared.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain how digital communications (e.g., email, text messages, chats) exposes business to risk

questions.question: Which of the following is a reason many travelers choose a destination for a business conference:

options.A: The number of museums in other cities
options.B: The local high school's sports team
options.D: The color of the hotel's carpets

questions.explanation: Easy access by air. Business travelers and meeting planners value convenience, so destinations with major airports, direct flights, and nearby hotels and convention centers are popular choices. Carpet colors, local school sports, and museums in other cities have little effect on where a conference is held. Understanding these motivations helps destinations and hotels market themselves to the right customers. Many cities build large convention centers near airports and hotels so they can attract conferences and the spending that comes with them.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain factors that motivate people to choose a hospitality and tourism site

questions.question: Why is a new restaurant usually considered a higher business risk than one that has operated successfully for many years?

options.B: It always pays more in taxes
options.C: It is not allowed to advertise

questions.explanation: It lacks loyal customers. New restaurants have no track record. They don't yet know how many customers will come, whether the menu will be popular, or whether costs will match their estimates. An established restaurant has loyal customers and years of experience that reduce uncertainty. New restaurants don't automatically pay more taxes and can advertise freely. Lenders and investors often view new businesses as riskier for these reasons. New restaurants can reduce risk by researching the local market, starting with a limited menu, and controlling costs carefully.

performanceIndicator.text: Determine factors affecting business risk

questions.question: Understanding personality types helps managers

options.A: assign tasks that fit employees' strengths.
options.C: label employees as good or bad workers.
options.D: make every employee act the same way.

questions.explanation: Assign tasks that fit employees' strengths. Personality type frameworks describe tendencies, such as preferring to work with people or to focus on details. Managers can use this information to match tasks with strengths, such as asking an outgoing employee to greet guests at an event and a detail-oriented one to manage reservations. Personality types aren't meant to label employees as good or bad, avoid people, or force everyone to behave alike. Understanding personality differences can also reduce conflict, because people learn why others work and communicate differently.

performanceIndicator.text: Leverage personality types in business situations

questions.question: For years, guests at the Linden Hotel have waited in line at the front desk to check out. Front desk agent Marisol suggests letting guests check out through a text message, and she shares data showing that most guests already use the hotel's text messaging service. Marisol is
questions.explanation: Challenging the status quo. Marisol is questioning a long-standing process and offering a specific, evidence-based alternative, which is a constructive way to challenge the status quo. She is not refusing her duties or ignoring policy; she is proposing a change through proper channels. Her idea is meant to make checkout easier for guests, not to create conflict. Supporting suggestions like this helps businesses stay competitive and keeps employees engaged. Constructive challengers explain the problem, offer a solution, and support it with facts.

performanceIndicator.text: Challenge the status quo

questions.question: A catering company plans to prepare 600 meals for a wedding. Which of the following is an input in this production process?
questions.explanation: The kitchen staff's labor. Inputs are the resources used to produce a good or service, such as labor, ingredients, equipment, and energy. The kitchen staff's work is a labor input. The guests' compliments, the photos, and thank-you cards come after the event and are not used to make the meals. Managing inputs carefully helps the caterer control costs and deliver consistent quality. Food, equipment, and energy are other inputs, while the finished meals are the outputs of the production process.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of production

questions.question: The Copper Spoon restaurant's sales stayed the same this year, but its profit fell because utility rates and insurance premiums rose. To improve profit, the owner should first

options.D: find ways to cut operating costs.

questions.explanation: Find ways to cut operating costs. The profit drop came from rising overhead, so reviewing those costs, such as switching to energy-efficient equipment or shopping for better insurance, addresses the problem directly. Stopping ingredient purchases would make the restaurant unable to operate, a 50% price increase would likely drive customers away, and closing on weekends would give up the busiest days. Managing overhead protects profit when sales don't grow. The owner could also review supplier contracts and staffing schedules to find other savings.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of overhead/operating costs

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a hotel using sales promotion:

options.B: Repainting the guest rooms on each floor

questions.explanation: Offering a third night free. Sales promotions are short-term incentives that encourage customers to buy, such as discounts, free nights, coupons, and contests. Training staff, repainting rooms, and hiring a chef may improve the guest experience, but they aren't promotional activities. Hotels often use promotions during slower seasons to fill rooms that would otherwise go unsold. Promotions should be planned carefully, though, because offering discounts too often can train guests to wait for deals instead of paying regular rates.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the concept of promotion in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A hotel that regularly asks guests to rate their stay and uses the results to improve service is practicing
questions.explanation: Quality management. Quality management involves setting standards, measuring performance, and continuously improving processes to meet customer expectations. Gathering guest ratings and acting on them is a key part of this cycle. Price discrimination involves charging different prices, inventory control manages supplies, and risk avoidance means not engaging in a risky activity. Quality management helps hospitality businesses deliver consistent experiences. Guest feedback often reveals problems that employees and managers don't notice. Hotels that act on feedback quickly can turn one-time guests into loyal customers.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of quality management

questions.question: Two guests stay in identical rooms at the same hotel on the same night. One raves about the friendly staff, while the other complains about rude service at check-in. This difference shows that hospitality products are
questions.explanation: Variable. Hospitality services are variable because quality depends on the people who provide them and the circumstances, so two guests can have very different experiences. Training and service standards help reduce variability. Services aren't durable, since they are used up as they are delivered, and they are intangible rather than tangible. The guests' different experiences show that the product was not identical. This is one reason hospitality businesses invest heavily in hiring and training front-line employees.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of product in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A hotel that improves its online reviews by training staff to resolve complaints quickly is most likely to see
questions.explanation: More bookings. Many travelers read reviews before booking, so better reviews make potential guests more confident and increase bookings. Resolving complaints quickly also builds loyalty among current guests. Better reviews usually attract, not reduce, website visitors, and training staff doesn't raise building costs. This shows how a company action, staff training, can lead to measurable business results. Hotels can track this connection by comparing review ratings with booking numbers over time. Responding publicly and politely to negative reviews can also show future guests that the hotel cares about solving problems.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate connections between company actions and results (e.g., influencing consumer buying behavior, gaining market share, etc.)

questions.question: A restaurant that turns raw ingredients into finished meals creates
questions.explanation: Form utility. Form utility is created when a business changes raw materials into a more useful product. Cooking ingredients into a meal makes them ready to eat and adds value for the customer. Place utility involves location, time utility involves availability when needed, and possession utility involves making it easier to own or use a product, such as accepting credit cards. A restaurant creates several utilities, but cooking is form utility. The restaurant also creates time utility by serving meals when customers want them and place utility through its location.

performanceIndicator.text: Determine economic utilities created by business activities

questions.question: A restaurant that sets lower prices for its lunch menu than for similar dinner items is most likely trying to

options.B: match the prices of grocery stores.
options.D: reduce the quality of its food.

questions.explanation: Attract more customers at lunch. Lunch customers often have less time and smaller budgets, and many restaurants are less busy at midday, so lower lunch prices encourage more people to come in. Prices are not meant to signal lower quality, the strategy aims to fill lunch seats rather than discourage dinner business, and restaurants don't usually set prices to match grocery stores. Pricing by time of day is common in hospitality. Restaurants may also offer smaller portions at lunch, which helps justify the lower prices.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of price in the hospitality and tourism industry

questions.question: A business owned by stockholders that has limited liability and can continue to exist after its founders leave is a
questions.explanation: Corporation. A corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners. Stockholders' liability is limited to what they invested, and the corporation continues even if owners sell their shares or the founders die. A sole proprietorship has one owner who is personally liable for its debts, a general partnership has two or more owners who share liability, and cooperatives are owned by members who use their services. Many large hotel and airline companies are corporations.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of business ownership

questions.question: Challenging the status quo at work means

options.C: keeping things exactly as they have always been.
options.D: refusing to follow any company rules.

questions.explanation: Questioning practices to improve them. The status quo is the way things are currently done. Challenging it means asking whether a process could be improved and proposing better ideas respectfully, often with evidence. It does not mean ignoring rules or complaining about everything, which damages relationships without improving anything. Keeping everything the same is the opposite of challenging the status quo. Many improvements in hospitality, such as mobile check-in, started with someone asking why a process had to stay the same.

performanceIndicator.text: Challenge the status quo

questions.question: A restaurant that serves fish labeled as fresh, local salmon when it is actually frozen imported fish is acting unethically because it

options.A: uses a freezer in its kitchen.
options.B: is buying supplies from a vendor.

questions.explanation: Misleads customers. Labeling a product falsely misleads customers who may pay more or choose the dish because they believe it is fresh and local. This is dishonest and may also violate truth-in-menu laws. Buying from vendors, using freezers, and selling seafood are normal operations. The ethical problem is the false description, not the product itself. Honest operations build trust and protect the restaurant's reputation. Accurate menu descriptions also help guests with allergies or dietary needs make safe choices.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the role of ethics in operations

questions.question: A hotel general manager needs to explain a new uniform policy that takes effect next month and that employees will need to review later. Which channel is most appropriate?

options.A: An email or memo with the details
options.C: A sticky note on the time clock
options.D: A brief comment in the hallway

questions.explanation: An email or memo with the details. A written message such as an email or memo provides a clear, permanent record that employees can review and refer to later. Hallway comments may be forgotten or misunderstood, a casual text with emojis may seem unprofessional and lack detail, and a sticky note can fall off or be missed. Many managers also discuss important changes in a meeting and then follow up in writing. Written policies also give managers a record showing that employees were informed of the change.

performanceIndicator.text: Choose and use appropriate channel for workplace communication

questions.question: Two restaurant servers argue loudly in the kitchen over who should take a large table. The manager wants to resolve the conflict. What should she do first?

options.C: Ignore it until the shift ends
options.D: Assign the table to the louder server

questions.explanation: Talk with both privately. Meeting privately allows each server to explain his or her view calmly, which helps the manager understand the cause and find a fair solution, such as a clear table-rotation policy. Rewarding the louder server encourages more conflict, ignoring it lets tension grow, and disciplining both before understanding the situation may be unfair. Fair, calm handling helps prevent future conflicts. Setting a clear rule for assigning tables afterward helps keep the same argument from happening again.

performanceIndicator.text: Use conflict-resolution skills

questions.question: Why do hospitality businesses create product extensions?

options.A: To reduce the number of products they offer
options.C: To attract new customers with related offerings

questions.explanation: To attract new customers with related offerings. Product extensions add new offerings related to an existing product, such as a hotel opening a spa or a restaurant selling meal kits. They help businesses reach new customers, increase spending by current customers, and make use of a well-known brand. Extensions increase rather than reduce the product mix, competitors still exist, and businesses usually keep their original products. Extensions do carry risk if the new offering doesn't match the brand's reputation.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of product extensions in the hospitality and tourism industry
